source.name: ECDC – European Respiratory Virus Surveillance Summary (ERVISS)
source.publisher: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), an EU agency
source.note: Figures are reported every week by the national public health institutes (FHI, Folkhälsomyndigheten and SSI) to ECDC, which publishes them openly every Friday. Recent weeks can be revised.

findings: Norway: 243 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 43 (+29% on the week before). Intensity: baseline (7% of an average season peak).
Sweden: 103 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 43 (+27% on the week before). Intensity: baseline (4% of an average season peak).
Denmark: 93 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 43 (−16% on the week before). Intensity: baseline (4% of an average season peak).
Highest influenza level: Norway, at 7% of an average season peak.
Dominant influenza virus so far this season (subtyped samples, all three countries): A(H1N1)pdm09 (85%).
COVID-19, lab-confirmed cases this week: Norway 232 (+39%, low); Sweden 121 (+42%, baseline); Denmark 71 (+27%, baseline).
RSV, lab-confirmed cases this week: Norway 6 (+50%, baseline); Sweden 4 (+300%, baseline); Denmark 0 (–, baseline).
Hospital and severity this week: Sweden 0 deaths with influenza; Sweden 4 deaths with COVID-19.
headline: Influenza: 439 lab-confirmed cases in the Nordics this week, up 16% on last week – baseline intensity (6% of an average season peak).
Nordics: COVID-19 424 cases (up 38%, baseline intensity); RSV 10 cases (up 100%, baseline intensity).
key_points: Highest influenza level: Norway, at 7% of an average season peak.
Dominant influenza virus so far this season (subtyped samples, all three countries): A(H1N1)pdm09 (85%).
Hospital and severity this week: Sweden 0 deaths with influenza; Sweden 4 deaths with COVID-19.

source.name: WHO FluNet – Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS)
source.note: Weekly influenza tests and positives reported by each country's National Influenza Centre to WHO. Recent weeks are often incomplete and are revised.

points: Australia's 2026 flu season has stayed below 10% test positivity: 9.1% in week 40, highest so far 9.6% (week 39) – medium (44% of an average peak); a late season (usually above 10% from week 24), mostly A(H3N2) (53% of subtyped samples).
Other southern-hemisphere seasons: New Zealand very high, Chile very high, South Africa high.
Dominant virus in the southern-hemisphere winter – a first hint of the mix for the Nordic one: Australia A(H3N2), New Zealand A(H1N1)pdm09, Chile B, South Africa A(H3N2).
No early-season market is above 10% influenza positivity yet (Japan, United States, Canada, England).
